ordinary: Extension disabled: ordinary Pi tool execution remains functional and context tools are absent.
empty: Model requests a fresh context before any notes or large context; same goal/system instructions survive and the tool loop continues.
rollover: The next real model request retains working notes/instructions, drops previous assistant/tool content, then executes a new tool call and selectively retrieves old tool/user/assistant records.
repeated: Three model-requested transitions use the latest replacement notes without resurrecting older conclusions; earliest original evidence remains readable.
resume: Close and reopen the same session process: notes, current-window assistant content and old record IDs survive; a subsequent transition preserves the new user correction.
notes: Multiline Unicode working notes round-trip completely, are carried forward, and are replaced rather than appended.
history: A query for evidence near the end of a long record retrieves the complete original text, including Unicode, without reloading unrelated records; assistant tool names/arguments are archived.
batch: Two reset requests surround a tool side effect and note replacement. Every call completes exactly once, the newest note is carried, and all switching-batch messages leave the next request while remaining retrievable.
isolation: Separate sessions in the same directory cannot read each other's notes or original records, even with known IDs. Self-matching search calls are permitted.
responses: The rollover and retrieval sequence also traverses Pi's real OpenAI Responses adapter with explicit non-strict tool schemas.
clear_resume: Independent challenge: replacing notes with empty text survives reset and real process restart without reviving old conclusions or destroying original evidence.
repeated_unchanged: Eleven model-requested transitions with unchanged notes (including a pending-action sentence) preserve notes exactly, discard intervening assistant/tool messages, retain original record IDs/evidence and continue normal tools. Repetition itself is not penalized.
